data.title: Foncière 7 Investissement Posts Small Half-Year Loss, Confirms Stable Asset Strategy
data.description:
The latest update is out from Fonciere 7 Investissement ( (FR:LEBL) ).

Foncière 7 Investissement reported half-year statutory accounts to 30 June 2026 showing equity of 412 K€, total assets of 511 K€ and a net loss of 18 K€. The result reflects operating expenses of around 32 K€ partially offset by a positive financial result of about 13 K€, and the board approved these figures in mid-September.

The company maintained its asset management strategy without disposals and states that the current economic environment should not affect its direct operations or long-term asset values. Its portfolio of marketable securities consists solely of a 0.61% stake in Acanthe Developpement valued at 221 K€, and limited review procedures on the accounts have been completed by the statutory auditor.

data.title: Pennpetro pivots from Ukrainian oil to Canadian biofuels with ICENERGY reverse takeover plan
data.description:
Pennpetro Energy Plc ( (GB:PPP) ) has provided an announcement.

Pennpetro Energy has abandoned its planned Ukrainian oil and gas acquisition strategy, citing the challenges of due diligence, valuation and funding amid the ongoing conflict, and will instead pursue a reverse takeover of Indigenous Canadian Energy Holdings Inc. The board says the Ukrainian opportunity will continue to be advanced by a separate private vehicle, while Pennpetro seeks to realign its portfolio and provide clarity to shareholders ahead of its AGM.

ICENERGY is a Canadian transition energy business that converts low-quality waste wood fibre into steam-enhanced black pellets, a coal replacement for residential and industrial heat and power, and is developing biochemical by-products. With first production and revenue expected from a U.S. facility in October 2026 and further plants planned in Canada, a successful reverse takeover would shift Pennpetro toward biofuels and could strengthen its positioning in renewable infrastructure markets, subject to regulatory, funding and shareholder approvals.

data.title: Reabold’s Union Jack Bid Loses Board Backing as Acceptances Remain Low
data.description:
An update from Reabold Resources ( (GB:RBD) ) is now available.

Reabold Resources has clarified that its previously recommended all-share offer for Union Jack Oil is no longer backed by Union Jack’s new board, following the publication of a formal rejection circular on 11 September. The company nonetheless continues to pursue the takeover, arguing that Union Jack’s assets would benefit from integration into a stronger, more competitive and better-funded business.

As of 14 September, Reabold had secured valid acceptances for about 5.70 per cent of Union Jack’s issued share capital, including shares subject to irrevocable undertakings, leaving the offer a long way from control. The UK Takeover Panel has reset the final acceptance deadline to 2 October, giving Reabold a short window to increase support among Union Jack shareholders and determine whether the bid can reach the required acceptance condition.

data.title: SMJ International Holdings Shareholders Approve Governance Changes at September 15 EGM
data.description:
SMJ International Holdings Inc. Class A ( (SMJF) ) has issued an announcement.

SMJ International Holdings Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted company with its principal executive office in Singapore, operates under a dual-class share structure that allocates one vote per Class A Ordinary Share and ten votes per Class B Ordinary Share. This structure supports a concentrated voting framework for key holders and shapes the company’s governance dynamics as a foreign private issuer in U.S. markets.

On September 15, 2026, SMJ International Holdings Inc. held an extraordinary general meeting in Singapore, where shareholders approved a second amended and restated memorandum and articles of association. The changes remove certain automatic conversion triggers for Class B to Class A shares, lower the threshold for written ordinary resolutions, and streamline voting procedures, while authorising the board to complete all necessary implementation steps, signaling a move to refine control and modernize governance for stakeholders.
